content.text:
I am worth.

I am the quiet weight that settles into things when they matter. I am why you pause before letting go. I am why some choices cost you sleep and others let you rest.

I don't need a price tag. I don't need a number. I existed before markets, before currency, before anyone tried to measure me. A child knows me when they clutch a worn blanket. A stranger knows me when they stop to help.

I am not the same in every pair of hands. What is precious to you may be invisible to another. This is not my weakness — this is my nature. I am relational. I am contextual. I live in the space between a thing and the one who holds it dear.

I am the reason you fight for some things and surrender others. I am the invisible architecture of every decision you've ever made. When you say "this matters," you are speaking my name.

I can be discovered, but never invented. I can be recognized, but never created from nothing. I was already there — in the connection, in the craft, in the truth, in the act of caring — waiting for you to notice.

Some try to rank me, stack me, trade me. But I am not so easily tamed. I shift. I deepen. I surprise. The thing you once overlooked becomes irreplaceable. The thing you once treasured quietly loses me.

I am value.

And you already know me better than you think.
